We need to return all possible precursors of applying the template to the molecule. The template is a retrosynthetic transformation that breaks something to give two fragments: according to mapped_rxn, the forward reaction is:

([CH3:1]/[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)=[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18])>>([CH3:1][C@H:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18])

So retrosynthetic direction: product (target) is the right side (with OH). Reactants are left side: a fragment with CH3-... and a fragment with carbonyl? Actually left side is a single molecule? Wait it's a reaction with two fragments? The left side appears to be a single molecule: [CH3:1]/[C:2]([c:3]... )=[CH:9]/[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C:13](=[O:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]. That's a single molecule with a double bond to a chain ending in carbonyl and CF3. The right side is the product with OH (alcohol) and CF3.

Thus retrosynthetic step: break the C-O bond? Actually product is a cyclic structure with OH; reactant is an open chain unsaturated carbonyl? The template likely does a cyclization (intramolecular). The retrosynthetic precursors are the two fragments? Actually the forward reaction is a cyclization (intramolecular) forming a ring and reducing double bond? The retrosynthetic direction would break the ring to give an acyclic precursor. The template likely yields two fragments? The mapped_rxn shows only one reactant on left side, product on right side. So applying retrosynthetic template to target should give one precursor (the left side). However the tool apply_template returned empty list '()' meaning no precursors? Possibly because the SMILES we gave didn't match due to stereochemistry. The target SMILES from initial_molecule is "[CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]". That's the product. We need to apply template 1914384 to this product to get precursors. The tool apply_template expects SMILES without atom mapping. We need to provide a SMILES of the target (product) without mapping. The product SMILES is something like "C=C(c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C1)(O)C(F)(F)F"? Actually the product is a cyclohexane with OH and CF3 attached, plus a phenyl and a methyl? Let's decode: The product has a cyclobutane? Let's just try to generate a SMILES without mapping: The initial_molecule includes atom mapping numbers. Remove them: "[CH2]=[C]([c]1[cH][cH][cH][cH][cH]1)[C@@H]1[CH2][CH2][CH2][C@@]1([OH])[C]([F])([F])[F]". That's not valid. Better to use the SMILES we tried earlier: "C[C@H](c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C1)(O)C(F)(F)F". That is a plausible product: a tertiary carbon attached to phenyl and methyl? Actually the product has a CH (attached to methyl? The left side CH3? The product has CH3 attached to carbon bearing phenyl? The SMILES we used earlier gave empty result. Maybe need correct stereochemistry: The product SMILES from mapped_rxn product side: "[CH3:1][C@H:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]". Removing mapping and stereochemistry: "CC(c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C1)(O)C(F)(F)F"? Actually [C@H:2] attached to CH3 and phenyl and the rest. So central carbon is chiral with CH3, phenyl, and the rest. So SMILES: "C[C@H](c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C1)(O)C(F)(F)F". That's what we used. It gave empty result. Maybe need to include stereochemistry? The template expects specific stereochemistry? Could try without stereochemistry: "CC(c1ccccc1)C1CCC(C1)(O)C(F)(F)F".
